meta_description: Run your own VPN on your own server: what you need, what it costs, and the four steps from an empty VPS to a working access key. Free and open-source.
page_desc: Run the VPN yourself instead of trusting somebody else's. VpnHood! is free and open-source, so the only thing standing between you and your own VPN is a server to put it on.
stack_desc: Every piece is free and open-source. The server is yours, and so is every byte that crosses it.
stack_manager_desc: The panel where you run it all: install servers, watch them live, and decide who gets access.
stack_server_desc: The engine of your VPN. It runs on your own Linux or Windows machine and carries your users' traffic on nobody's infrastructure but yours.
stack_client_desc: The app your users install. They paste the access key you give them, and they are connected.
need_desc: Less than you might think. There is nothing to buy from us.
need_server_desc: Any VPS or dedicated machine running Linux or Windows. This is the one thing that costs money, and you pay your cloud provider, not us.
need_account_desc: It is the sign-in for VpnHood! MANAGER, the free panel that installs and runs your servers for you.
need_skills_desc: The install is a single command you paste, or you can hand the panel an SSH login and let it do the work.
need_domain_desc: Own one and you get a free, automatically renewed TLS certificate; skip it and a self-signed certificate works fine.
steps_title: Four steps to a working VPN
step1_desc: Open VpnHood! MANAGER and sign in with your Google account.
step2_desc: Follow the install steps to put VpnHood! SERVER on your machine.
step3_desc: Issue a key from the Access Token page, with the limits you choose.
step4_desc: Anyone with VpnHood! CLIENT pastes it in and is connected.
manual_note: Rather not use the panel at all? VpnHood! SERVER also runs on its own — install it manually on Windows, Linux, or Docker (opens in new tab).
cta: Your VPN, your server, your rules — and the first access key is only minutes away.
